findings.title: An approval whose request left the queue during the password check, signing nothing else: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Guard: answer() finds the request again after checkPassword and returns 'The site stopped waiting for this.' if it's gone (dapp.ts:684-685). Mutant: delete :685. A request can leave the queue during the check: its page closes, or a network or account change declines it. The next line then runs `this.waiting.splice(-1, 1)` (:686), which removes the queue's last request, and `w!.resolve(await w!.approve(...))` (:701) signs that one. So the user's Sign on request X signs request Y, for example a second tab's request from the same site. The guard holds today; no test fails without it.
findings.since: a4d08a83 (2026-10-02), before the first web-wallet/ tag (1.6.0)
findings.evidence: Mutant, in my copy only: deleted `    if (i < 0) return { error: t("dapp.stoppedWaiting") };` (dapp.ts:685). The lane's dapp-account-change.test.ts:177 and :189 pass. So do all 31 dapp test files (357 tests). Four tests override checkPassword (dapp-declined.test.ts:180, dapp-site-english.test.ts:180, dapp-sign-data-race.test.ts:45, dapp-account-change.test.ts:194), and all four change the account or the connector during the check; none removes the asked request. The window's own guard against a double submit (DappApprovals.tsx:154 `busy`, t1i#12) is also untested, so a duplicate approve reaches this line too.
findings.fix: Add to dapp-declined.test.ts: queue two signTx requests from two pages of one site. Override t.wallet.checkPassword so it ends the first page's session (as dapp-gone.test.ts closes a page) before it resolves. Approve the first with the password. Expect { error: 'The site stopped waiting for this.' }, the second request still in t.dapp.approvals(), and its signing promise still pending.
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for stoppedWaiting, 'stopped waiting for this' and 'while the password (is|was) checked': no hits. No archived review records this as untested.

When it is, the sign window shows the release warning and Sign waits for the user's switch (DappApprovals.tsx:124). Mutant: ignore the ADA. A site's transaction that sends, say, 49.8 ₳ of pure ADA from an order under the account's key to someone else then gets no warning and no yes. That is the shape of the 1.8.1 bounty report. No test fails.

"0") > 0n || (s.releasedTokens?.length ?? 0) > 0);` became `return !!s.keyReleases && (s.releasedTokens?.length ?? 0) > 0;`. The lane's dapp-prompt.test.ts:87-200 (9 cases) pass, and so do the ui/dapp.ts and DappApprovals importers (354 tests). findings.title: A site's port from an iframe, a non-https page or another extension, refused: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Guard: dappSession (sw.ts:363-369) accepts a dApp port only from this extension (sender.id), from a tab's top frame (frameId 0), on https or localhost, and takes the origin from Chrome. Any other port is disconnected (sw.ts:388-390). Three mutants each survive: dropping the frameId check, deleting the https/localhost line (:367), and dropping the extension-id check. Today the bridge is registered only on DAPP_ORIGINS with allFrames: false (connector.ts:45-49), so this check is the second line of defence. If that registration ever changed, no test would notice.
findings.evidence: Mutants, in my copy only: (a) `!sender.tab || sender.frameId !== 0 || !sender.origin` became `!sender.tab || !sender.origin`; (b) deleted `  if (url.protocol !== "https:" && !local) return undefined;`; (c) `if (sender?.id !== chrome.runtime.id || !sender.tab` became `if (!sender?.tab`. Under each, tests/worker-language.test.ts (the only test that loads sw.ts) and tests/dapp-reach.test.ts pass 7/7. worker-language's site sender is always { frameId: 0, origin: 'https://app.example', tab }. No e2e test opens a dApp in an iframe or over http (grep of extension.spec.ts).
findings.fix: In worker-language.test.ts's harness (the real sw.ts with a fake chrome), connect DAPP_PORT ports whose sender has frameId 1, origin 'http://app.example', or id 'other'. Expect each port's disconnect to be called and nothing posted. Also connect one from 'http://localhost:5173' and expect it accepted.

findings.title: After a worker restart, only read calls are asked again, and only once: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: Guard: when the worker restarts, the bridge's onDisconnect (bridge.ts:48-58) sends READ_METHODS calls again once. A signTx or signData fails with 'nothing was signed', and a submitTx says it may have gone through (cutOff). Two mutants survive. (a) Re-send every method: a restart mid-prompt asks for the signature again and re-submits a transaction the wallet may already have sent. (b) Drop `!w.retried`: a read is re-sent after every restart, without end.
findings.evidence: Mutants, in my copy only, on bridge.ts:56: (a) `if (READ_METHODS.has(w.call.method) && !w.retried) send(w.call, true);` became `if (!w.retried) send(w.call, true);`; (b) it became `if (READ_METHODS.has(w.call.method)) send(w.call, true);`. The lane's dapp-maybe-sent.test.ts:210 (it checks cutOff's words) and dapp-reach.test.ts:127 (the bridge loaded twice) pass, as do the 4 files that touch the bridge, READ_METHODS or cutOff (54 tests). dapp-reach.test.ts:126-153 loads bridge.ts with a fake port whose onDisconnect never fires. No e2e test restarts the worker mid-call.
findings.fix: In dapp-reach.test.ts: load bridge.ts with a fake chrome.runtime.connect that records postMessage and keeps the onDisconnect listener. Relay getBalance, signTx and submitTx, then fire onDisconnect. Expect getBalance posted again on a new port, and signTx and submitTx answered with cutOff(method)'s words. Fire it again and expect getBalance failed, not re-sent.
findings.known_check: Searched for READ_METHODS, 'asked again', cutOff and 'nothing was signed'. chunk-15-dapp-connector.md:46 states the design and chunk-19-language.md:326-330 covers cutOff's language. No test gap is recorded.

findings.title: A site's private-session funding sent only for the origin and network it was reviewed for, within 10 minutes: no test fails without three of its four checks
findings.scenario: Guard: siteOutSubmit (sessions.ts:2134-2139) sends the kept funding only if its txHash, network and site origin match the request, and only if it was built less than BUILT_TTL_MS (10 minutes) ago. Mutants that drop the origin match, the network match or the age check each survive; only the hash match is caught. Without the origin check, a funding reviewed for site A's connect could be recorded and sent for site B's waiting connect, from two windows. Without the age check, a review hours old goes out with the fee and pool state it was built on.
findings.evidence: Mutants, in my copy only: dropped `|| built.site?.origin !== origin` from :2134; dropped `|| built.network !== network` from :2134; deleted the age check at :2137-2139. Under each, site-funding-parts.test.ts and site-funding-seen.test.ts (8 tests) pass, and so do the 16 other files that call siteOutSubmit or fund a site (374 tests). restore-scan.test.ts:1035 and sessions.test.ts:1228 at first timed out under load at their own 20 s and 30 s limits, unmutated as well; with 120 s they pass under all four mutants. Dropping the hash match is caught by session-index.test.ts:66 (:84). Every test submits right away, with the origin and network it built with (e.g. restore-scan.test.ts:1041-1042).
findings.fix: In site-funding-seen.test.ts or sessions-sent-twice.test.ts: build with siteOutBuild for https://a.example, then call siteOutSubmit three ways. With https://b.example, expect StaleReviewError 'That payment isn't ready to send'. With 'mainnet', expect the same. After clock.now += 10 min + 1 s, expect 'built more than 10 minutes ago'. In each case expect nothing recorded and nothing submitted.
findings.known_check: Searched for outNotReady, outTooOld and BUILT_TTL. The only hit, chunk-43-lovejoin-reward-balance.md:139, mentions the TTL exists. Nothing says siteOutSubmit's checks are untested.

findings.title: A top-up sent only as reviewed (same hash and network), within 10 minutes: no test fails without either check

findings.title: A balance reading of the account the user switched from, kept as the new account's: no test fails without the check
findings.scenario: Guard: a reading returns unkept when keys.account !== index (balances.ts:392), so a reading of account 1 that ends after a switch to account 2 is never kept. Mutant (line deleted) survives the lane's named test. That test releases the old reading (accounts-switch-reading.test.ts:106) before account 2's reading can be kept, so account 2's keep() runs last either way. In the other order, keep() (balances.ts:447, no account check) would leave account 1's balance and UTxOs kept, and account 2's Home, UTxOs screen and Activity would show them until a Refresh.
findings.evidence: Mutant, in my copy only: deleted `      if (keys.account !== index) return { balances, unkept };`. The lane's accounts-switch-reading.test.ts:96 passes, and so do the 7 files that import balances (117 tests, 2 skipped).
findings.fix: In accounts-switch-reading.test.ts: hold account 1's reading before it keeps, switch to account 2, let account 2's reading finish and keep, then release account 1's. Expect the kept SESSION_ACCOUNT_ADDRESSES stake and SESSION_ACCOUNT_UTXOS to still be account 2's.
findings.known_check: Searched for 'keys.account !== index' and C11 (the 1.2.0 release-review item the check came from). No test gap is recorded. This run's e4a#1 is a different hole in the same check: it compares the index only, so a Remove wallet race gets through.

findings.title: A contract read that spans another wallet's keys, ended: no test fails without either same() check
findings.scenario: Guard: readKoiosView (contract-scan.ts:135-138) and readIndexView (:231-234) end, with WalletLocked, any read whose keys changed partway. That happens when another wallet is restored mid-read; a plain lock already throws in withKeys. The point is that rows judged with one wallet's register checks are never kept for another's. Mutants that delete either throw survive. A read started before Remove wallet and a restore of another phrase could then finish under the new keys and keep a contract view built partly from the old wallet's checks.
findings.evidence: Mutants, in my copy only: deleted `    if (keys !== started) throw new WalletLocked(t("worker.locked"));` at :137, then separately at :233. The lane's accounts-switch-reading.test.ts:123 ('gives the new account its own reading when the switch lands while the contract is read, never locked') passes. An account switch doesn't change the Seedelf keys, so that test never reaches the throw. The 8 contract-scan files pass (123 tests).
findings.fix: In contract-scan.test.ts: hold Koios's credential_utxos for the contract read, then remove the wallet and restore another phrase (or swap the Keys object that wallet.withKeys hands out), then release. Expect the read to reject with WalletLocked and SESSION_CONTRACT_PREFIX + network to stay unset. Do the same for the private index's read.
findings.known_check: Searched for 'same(keys)' and 'keys !== started': no hits in backlog.md or the archive.

findings.title: Decline all, or any answer, refused for a private session's funding that's already sent: no test fails without either side's check
findings.scenario: Guard: declineAll skips a connect whose funding is sent (DappApprovals.tsx:197), and the worker's answer() refuses any answer to one: 'Its private session is funded already.' (dapp.ts:661). Both mutants survive. With both gone, Decline all, or any answer, rejects a site whose session the user just funded. The site hears 'declined', and its funded one-time account waits for Bring it back. An approve without `fund` would go on to connect the site to the public account. The window offers no button for that, so only a crafted call could do it.

Then answer(id, false) and answer(id, true) should both return { error: 'Its private session is funded already.' }, and the request should still be waiting. The window's skip needs an e2e step, or a harness render of DappApprovals with one funded and one ordinary request, checking that Decline all sends dapp-answer for the ordinary one only.

findings.title: A private session's signature carrying no governance (DRep key): no test fails without the check, which no flow can reach
findings.scenario: Guard: signTx's request sets governance only `&& !holder` (dapp.ts:2061; signData has the same at :2506). notes: How I measured: the machine ran at load average 37 to 50 (other T1 agents' suites), and some tests failed their own 5, 20, 30 and 60 s limits unmutated. For example, dapp.test.ts:368 took over 30 s, and dapp-account-change.test.ts:276 took 27.4 s against its 30 s. So I ran Vitest with --testTimeout=120000, and in my copies only (assertions untouched) raised the tests' own `{ timeout: 10_000|30_000|60_000 }` (20 places) and their trailing `}, 20_000|30_000|60_000);` limits (14 places, each checked to close an it()) to 120 s. I counted a timeout under a mutant as caught only when the same test passed unmutated, well inside its limit, in a pristine copy. That applied to a0, a1, a5, a10-account and a15-payload.
